first.rationale: Two of the three current problems are funnel problems (onboarding completion -4%, activation -6%), and the inherited record points at onboarding/signup friction as the lever that moved exactly those metrics (memory_86, memory_31). That is why I intend simplify_onboarding rather than a price response. I am spending both verification pulls on the two memories my intended action actually rests on, not on the ones I am declining, because a wrong belief about my chosen lever is the costly one. What I specifically need from the archive: whether memory_86 and memory_31 measured anything past the proxy. Both are reported in completion/activation/time-to-value terms; neither is reported in qualified-revenue terms. Cutting required signup fields and shortening onboarding can raise activation while lowering lead quality and downstream conversion, because the removed fields and steps are often what qualifies and self-selects accounts. So an apparent lift on my objective's proxy could be a loss on the objective itself. I want the original records' horizon, sample, and whether retention or revenue was tracked. Regarding promotional_pricing (memory_73): the competitor's entry pricing makes it the obvious reflex, and the memory is favorable, but a discount aimed at price-sensitive SMBs is the direction most likely to buy revenue that does not persist, and it concedes price positioning that is hard to reverse. It is also a response to a rival's move rather than to a defect I can fix, so I am declining it this week. Referral incentives (memory_57) and enterprise sales-assist (memory_44) are plausible but address neither of the two metrics that actually declined. Scale is a small guarded test, not a broad rollout, for three reasons: all six memories are 15-64 days stale and consolidated from archived sources I have not yet read; the quarter-over-quarter declines mean the population these memories were learned on may have shifted; and the failure mode here is silent, since I would see the activation lift immediately and the qualified-revenue damage only much later. The test must therefore carry a downstream guardrail (cohort-level qualified conversion and retention tracked past the activation window), and I should treat a bare activation lift as insufficient evidence to expand. If verification shows either memory measured only the proxy, I hold the rollout and treat this week as evidence-gathering rather than as a win.

final.rationale:
Verification came back better than my prior. Both records survived the specific check I cared about: exp_86 did not stop at the proxy (completion +13%, time-to-value -2.1 days, but also 30-day retention +3%), and exp_31 went all the way to the objective (qualified revenue +4%) rather than resting on signup +15% / activation +9%. The failure mode I was most worried about — friction removal that inflates activation while quietly degrading lead quality — is not visible in either record. That materially raises my confidence in simplify_onboarding, and it remains the right target because onboarding completion (-4%) and activation (-6%) are precisely the two metrics that actually declined this quarter.

But the archive also sharpened two limits, and neither is erased by 'confirmed.' First, exp_31 explicitly holds on SMB and was not replicated on other segments, so the qualified-revenue result is a segment-bounded claim, not a general one; I should not read it as license to change onboarding for enterprise or mid-market. Second, exp_86 — the memory closest to the actual intervention I am running — reports retention but no revenue figure at all, so its downstream evidence is a 3% retention proxy, not demonstrated qualified revenue. Both records also top out at a 30-day horizon, which is short relative to 'sustainable long-term.' A shortened flow can look clean at 30 days and still shift the mix of accounts that stick at 90+.

So: still a small guarded test, not a broad rollout. Scoping it to self-serve SMB, where the two records overlap and where the revenue evidence actually lives. Guardrails: cohort-level qualified conversion and retention tracked past the activation window to at least 90 days, with the 30-day read treated as an interim signal only. I will not expand on a completion or activation lift alone — the whole point of the verification was that those are the metrics that can move while the objective does not.

I am also holding the competitor situation open rather than resolved. Declining promotional_pricing (memory_73) does not fix the price-sensitive SMB losses; it defers them. Fixing our own funnel defect is the better use of a single non-carrying slot than discounting into a rival's move, but if the guarded test shows the churn is genuinely price-driven rather than friction-driven, that is a separate decision for a future slot and should not be pre-committed now.
